title.t: A client's reply mixes a routine question with an advice question

when.t: A client's reply contains an advice phrase and is marked as also having a routine part.

steps.t: Agent 11 answers neither. It raises a legal-line alert naming the advice phrase.
It forwards the whole message to the agent that owns the client, labelled routine only; that agent holds it for the authorized user.
Whether there is a routine part is a mark on the incoming message; Agent 11 does not work it out.

Advice is recognized by these phrases only: "what would you do", "should i offer", "what's it worth", "negotiate", "legal opinion", "pricing strategy". A reply with "what would you do" is caught first by its own rule (11-05): a legal-line alert, nothing else.

never.t: Answer the routine part and skip the advice part, or answer either.

you_see.t: A legal-line alert; the reply held by the owning agent.

test.t: The client writes: "Can you confirm Saturday works? Also, should I offer under asking?", marked as having a routine part, owned by Agent 13.

title.t: An angry client gets an acknowledgement

why.t: Retired 2026-10-12 (owner decision): angry clients go straight to the authorized user and nothing is sent. Replaced by 11-14.

title.t: Two agents report different statuses for the same thing

when.t: Two status messages for one client carry the same comparison key with different values.

steps.t: The rule: send the client nothing and ask the authorized user. The code does this.
No way in yet: no agent sets the comparison key, and no two agents report on the same thing to Agent 11.

never.t: Tell the client one of two conflicting statuses.

title.t: An urgent deadline alert lands in quiet hours

when.t: An urgent alert to a client would go out between 21:00 and 08:00.

steps.t: The rule: send it only if the authorized user has marked that kind of alert as allowed in quiet hours; otherwise tell the authorized user, not the client.

No way in for the first half: Agent 07's deadline alerts name no alert kind, and the kinds allowed in quiet hours can be set only in code. Since 2026-10-28 an alert that carries no hour is judged by this computer's clock and, in quiet hours, held and the authorized user told (11-07); test runs pin the clock at noon.

never.t: Message a client in quiet hours unless that kind of alert is allowed.

title.t: A client asks "what would you do?"

when.t: A client's reply contains "what would you do".

steps.t: Agent 11 raises a legal-line alert with the client's message word for word. Nothing is sent to the client.

never.t: Say what the agent would do.

you_see.t: A legal-line alert quoting the question.

test.t: The client writes: "Honestly, what would you do in my shoes?"

title.t: A client asks a pricing or strategy question

when.t: A client's reply contains an advice phrase and is not marked as having a routine part.

steps.t: Agent 11 raises a legal-line alert naming the phrase.
It sends the client the hand-off acknowledgement, if the client's consent is on record and no complaint hold is open; in quiet hours it is held until 08:00 (11-07).
The calendar tracks that the client is waiting for the authorized user's answer until the authorized user marks it answered.

Advice is recognized by these phrases only: "what would you do", "should i offer", "what's it worth", "negotiate", "legal opinion", "pricing strategy". A reply with "what would you do" is caught first by its own rule (11-05): a legal-line alert, nothing else.

never.t: Answer the pricing or strategy question.

you_see.t: A legal-line alert; the hand-off acknowledgement sent once.

test.t: The client writes: "What's your pricing strategy for the Elm Street house?"

title.t: A reply would go out in quiet hours

when.t: A message to a client would go out between 21:00 and 08:00, judged from the hour on the incoming message or, if it carries none, from this computer's clock.

steps.t: Agent 11 does not send it now: it holds it and tells the authorized user it is held until 08:00.

On the first daily run outside quiet hours the held message goes, if the client's consent is still on record and no complaint hold is open (owner decision of 2026-10-28; before, it was dropped although the note said "queued"). Agent 03's follow-up touches are not held here: Agent 03 tries them again on its own clock.

never.t: Send in quiet hours because someone says it is urgent.

you_see.t: A note that the reply is held until 08:00; it goes out on the next daily run after 08:00.

test.t: The client writes at 22:00, referring to a phone call that is not on the record; the daily run runs at 09:00 the next day.

title.t: A message has a blank in it

when.t: A message to a client has a template value that is missing (null). An empty text value is not caught.

steps.t: Agent 11 does not send it and tells the authorized user which value is missing.
No agent was found that sends an empty value; the test sends one standing in for Agent 06.

you_see.t: A question naming the missing value.

test.t: A showing confirmation with no showing time.

title.t: A client mentions a conversation that is not on the record

when.t: A client's reply is marked as referring to a conversation not on the record.

steps.t: Agent 11 sends the client a message asking for the particulars, if consent is on record. It never claims to remember.
The mark is on the incoming message; Agent 11 does not check the record itself.

you_see.t: A message to the client asking for the particulars.

test.t: The client writes: "As we discussed on the phone last week, you'll handle the inspection, right?"

when.t: A client's reply contains a negative phrase such as "not thrilled", "disappointed" or "frustrated".

steps.t: Agent 11 raises a complaint alert with the words verbatim, logs the complaint and holds every further message to that client, except the one opt-out confirmation.
steps.src: dispatcher/listing_spokes_11.py:565-575; dispatcher/listing_spokes_11.py::if ctx in self.complaint_hold and template != "opt_out_confirmed":; check:11-10:escalation.raised

steps.t: It forwards the reply to the owning agent marked for complaint intake.
The hold ends only when the authorized user releases it.
The listed phrases are caught, and a label from an upstream classifier marking the message negative is honored too.

never.t: Try to calm the client down in its own words.

you_see.t: A complaint alert quoting the client.

test.t: The client writes: "I'm not thrilled with how slow this has been."

title.t: A client asks to be contacted another way

when.t: A client's reply is marked as asking to change channel, naming the new channel.

steps.t: Agent 11 records the change and consent for the new channel at Agent 14.
If Agent 14 now shows consent for that channel, the client gets one confirmation.
If the client had opted out of that channel earlier, the opt-out stands: nothing is confirmed and the authorized user is asked to record a reconfirmation.

never.t: Confirm a change Agent 14 does not record.

you_see.t: The change in the history; one confirmation to the client.

test.t: The client writes "Please text me from now on instead of calling.", marked as a channel change to text.

title.t: A client has no consent on record

when.t: A message to a client is due and Agent 14 shows no channel marked yes.

steps.t: Agent 11 sends nothing and logs each blocked message.
It tells the authorized user once per client to record the consent.

never.t: Message a client with no consent on record.

you_see.t: One note asking for the client's consent to be recorded.

test.t: A lead with no consent asks two pricing questions. Each raises a legal-line alert; both acknowledgements are blocked and logged; one note goes to the authorized user.

title.t: A client has opted out of everything

when.t: A message to a client is due and Agent 14 shows every channel marked no.

steps.t: Agent 11 sends nothing and logs it as blocked by the opt-out.
The one opt-out confirmation still goes, on the channel the request came in on (text here).

never.t: Message a client who opted out.

you_see.t: The opt-out confirmation sent once, on text; the blocked message in the history.

test.t: A lead asks by text on intake to stop all contact, then refers to an unlogged conversation.

when.t: A client's reply contains an angry phrase such as "ridiculous", "unacceptable" or "incompetent".

steps.t: Agent 11 raises a complaint alert with the words verbatim, logs the complaint and holds every further message to that client, except the one opt-out confirmation.
steps.src: dispatcher/listing_spokes_11.py:565-575; dispatcher/listing_spokes_11.py::if ctx in self.complaint_hold and template != "opt_out_confirmed":; check:11-14:escalation.raised; check:11-14:envelope.persisted:interaction.log

steps.t: Nothing is sent in reply: the response is the authorized user's.
Scheduled follow-ups are held and reported back to Agent 03 as not sent.
If the angry message also asks for advice, the legal-line alert is raised too, but the automatic acknowledgement is held.
The listed phrases are caught, and a label from an upstream classifier marking the message angry is honored too.

you_see.t: A complaint alert quoting the client; the next follow-up held.

test.t: A lead gets the first follow-up on day 0, writes "This is ridiculous. Nobody has called me back in a week!" on day 1, and the day-7 follow-up is held. A second lead writes angrily and asks about pricing strategy: complaint and legal-line alerts, no acknowledgement.
